prize_parts.citation: for showing how differences between firms and their selection into exporting shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed: I now prefer B048 over B001, which I preferred in round 1. In round 1 I called the gap small and said I would take B048 seriously. The exchange has settled it for me on two grounds. First, the discovery is cleaner. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable originating model, and Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI makes the second name natural. Credit divides more cleanly than in B001, where the cap excludes Vishny, a co-author of the founding papers. Second, robustness. The qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data for more than twenty years and have largely held up. In round 1 I argued that B001's lasting contribution is making legal institutions measurable, and I still think that has value. But the colleagues who stressed coding, endogeneity of legal origin and the law-versus-history question are right that this is the part a citation would have to rest on. A citation limited to data and research design would be defensible but thin. As a macroeconomist who works with calibrated models, I weigh a mechanism that is tied to data and has survived testing more heavily than a research programme whose central causal claim is qualified. The 2008 prize rewarded earlier new trade theory with representative firms, and I do not treat it, or field rotation, as evidence against this work. Under common criteria the comparison should rest on discovery, attribution and maturity.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the main weakness. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed parallel firm-level facts and models, and none is on the ballot entry. A Melitz-Helpman credit can be read as favouring the theory over the empirical foundations, and the cap of three names cannot resolve this. Welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. Helpman's separate appearance in another package (B026) is unresolved and could affect how the citation is framed. Moving from B001 to B048 also means giving up my own judgement that creating a new field is somewhat more decisive than refining an established one. I now see that as insufficient when the strongest claim of the field-creating work is contested. Finally, as chair I am aware that my round-1 preference was counted among the B001 supporters, so I state the change openly and do not treat it as a concession to a majority. Support counts are not merit.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B001 seventh. She argues that its influence exceeds the strength of its evidence, citing measurement, coding and causal identification of the legal-origins indices, and she ranks B048 first for testable predictions that have survived replication.
responses.response: In round 1 I accepted the substance of her critique, and in round 2 it carries more weight with me. The strong causal form of the legal-origins thesis is not established, so a citation could not honestly endorse it. If the citation has to be reduced to data and research design, it is weaker than a citation for a mechanism whose core predictions have held up across many datasets. On the evidence about what survived testing, I now side with her ordering of B048 over B001.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson moved from B001 to B048 because of the identification problem. She calls the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line the real vulnerability for B048, since it concerns priority on the empirical foundations, and she would word the citation around the selection mechanism.
responses.response: I agree with both parts. Her move reflects the same weighing I have now made. I also accept that the priority question is not a technicality. It answers one of the chair's questions: a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains from trade is adequate to what Melitz and Helpman established, and it avoids claiming credit for the firm-level facts. I do not think this priority risk should change my preference, because B001 carries a comparable attribution cost (Vishny), plus the contested causal claim. I would still want the committee to state the limitation openly.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B037 first for Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler. He would accept a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize if Gertler's credit is judged too entangled with B040, and he argues the 2022 prize addressed banks and crises, not collateral amplification.
responses.response: I agree with him on the scientific standing of Kiyotaki-Moore. It is a mature, clean amplification mechanism, and I keep B037 as an alternative. I find his distinction between the 2022 prize and the collateral mechanism fair, so overlap reduces marginal novelty and does not disqualify. Two things keep it below B048 for me. Attribution still depends on whether Gertler is included. And, as he acknowledges, the empirical identification of collateral channels is weaker than the theory's influence. He is my frequent co-author and IIES colleague, so I note that this is a judgement on the merits, and the tie is disclosed, not adjudicated. I would not move him toward B048 on the strength of my view alone.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B001 first. He argues the critiques qualify the mechanism more than they undermine the discovery, and that a prize can recognise founding a field even if the first causal story is partly wrong. He would word the citation around the research design and regularities.
responses.response: This is close to my own round-1 position, and I still find the field-founding point serious. We differ on how much the committee should rest on it. A citation that avoids the causal legal-origins claim leaves the credited achievement as measurement and regularities. That is a real contribution, but it is harder to defend as a discovery than a mechanism with tested predictions. The Vishny cost also remains. I have therefore moved B001 to my first alternative. If the committee prefers B001 with careful wording, I would not oppose it as a serious outcome. I would want the citation to avoid the strong causal reading.

responses.point: Fredriksson cites my round-1 ranking of B015 as eighth and my maturity objection. He rejects the maturity point because the China-shock papers are about a decade old and persistence is confirmed, but concedes my attribution point and moves to B048.
responses.response: I accept part of his reply on maturity. Ten years is enough for the core effects to be documented, and I should not have framed it as simply immature. My concern is that the long-run magnitude and persistence are still being measured. The attribution problem remains the stronger argument against B015: the Katz-versus-Dorn choice and the task-framework lineage outside the ballot. I do not place B015 among my two alternatives, because B001 and B037 have the clearer credit structures.

uncertainties: Whether a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism is enough if the committee judges the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority question material.
How Helpman's appearance in B026 affects his claim and the framing here, which I treat as an unresolved issue, not a reason to discount him.
How much the welfare conclusions depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity.
Whether I now underweight the field-creating value of B001, since my change of preference rests partly on a judgement about robustness over influence that colleagues reasonably contest.
Whether Gertler's credit in B037 can be separated from B040 and the 2022 prize, which affects how strong an alternative B037 is.
All assessments rest on my own recollection of the literature and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Melitz or Helpman, or to the credited names on B001 or B037, is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose, without adjudicating, co-authorship and institutional ties with committee colleagues Per Krusell (frequent co-author and IIES colleague, who prefers B037, one of my alternatives), Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg. I am the chair, and my round-1 preference for B001 was counted in the chair's summary. My preference has changed to B048. My field is macroeconomics, which is not the field of the candidate I now prefer.
